scope: Independent read-only source and scoped closed-history audit of a separate physical reach-row pitch rounded to eight f32 values, against accepted E020. This preserves completed findings; no new investigation or experiment is authorized by this report.

findings.finding: No hidden continuation or save-layout blocker found. Paging and stored continuation record actual device slice lengths, borrow/swap whole buffers, check sufficient capacity and synchronize before release. Parked and checkpointed state contains only four regret/strategy arrays, not reach rows.

Exact reach-byte accounting must use physical pitch in the plan, two existing device allocations, public VRAM estimate and stored-capacity planner. Existing research_capacity_check compares metadata and state, not predicted workspace-component bytes against actual lengths.

Additional resident and zero-initialized payload is 4*sum(reach_blocks[p]*(pitch[p]-nh[p])) bytes in the two existing buffers. This increases constructor zero-fill/workspace cost and may change budget admission or full-versus-compact action layout selection. No cost or gain was measured.

Logical nh must remain unchanged for loops, regret/sigma indexing, shared memory, normalization and saved layouts. Five kernels address reach rows: down_action, down_chance, up_fold, up_show and training up_action. Root physical slot zero remains unchanged. Deriving zero pitch from E015 down_nh1=0 is safe only while the existing zero logical loops prevent reach memory access.

Existing reach lifecycle checks compare entire buffers within the same compiled layout and include poisoned workspace/changed-root cases. They remain useful for dispatch consistency but do not establish original-layout versus padded-layout raw-vector equality, since lengths and row offsets differ.

No direct reach-pitch duplicate was found in the scoped postflop ledger and archived design-note search. E025 changed only CFV physical stride and was rejected at 0.9378% slower. D038/D039 global-gather designs explicitly retained nh_o reach stride. D049 pointer selection and E026 physical showdown width are distinct rejected work. None supplies evidence that reach padding improves complete-cycle time.

limitations: Scoped history search, not an exhaustive audit of every older experiment.
Source feasibility only; no allocation, compiler, arithmetic differential, GPU or complete-cycle validation was run.
No new experiment, test matrix, implementation or performance acceptance is proposed by this preservation note.
